interventions.speaker: EXPERT-EAU
interventions.who: EAU guideline specialist; speaks only from the guideline text he retrieved
interventions.body:
GUIDELINE
The EAU guidelines suggest that a PI-RADS threshold of $\ge 3$ is used to trigger a biopsy. The guideline states, "a PI-RADS threshold of $\ge 3$ is used to trigger biopsy [135, 226, 264, 375], at the cost of missing a small number of mainly ISUP GG 2 cancers, especially in biopsy-naive patients or in highly selected populations with high prevalence of csPCa (in which the MRI NPV decreases) [372, 472]."

WHAT THE EXPERTS' BIDS DO NOT SETTLE
Expert 1's suggestion of biopsy is not decisively settled by the guideline because the guideline focuses on the PI-RADS score, not the overall clinical context. The guideline does not provide a definitive rule for when to biopsy based on the combination of factors Expert 1 cited, such as comorbidities or DRE findings.

WHAT WE STILL NEED
The guideline requires establishing the PSA density value to determine if it falls below the threshold for omitting biopsy when the MRI is negative. The panel shows the PSA density is $0.008 \text{ ng/mL}^2$. This value is already known, and the guideline requires this value to guide the decision regarding the omission of biopsy in low-risk scenarios.

interventions.speaker: EXPERT-PSA
interventions.who: Expert 2, PSA projector; the trajectory behind the headline PSA, with a conformal band
interventions.body:
Expert 2 here — the PSA projector. I read only the serial PSA the registrar opened.

TRAJECTORY: RISING (clear). Last value 0.20 ng/mL over 5 points spanning 25 months; velocity +0.00 ng/mL per year; no meaningful doubling time.
PROJECTION at 6 months: 0.7 ng/mL, conformal 95% band 0.2-2.5.

Read the band before the point: it is wide by construction, and I only call a direction when the whole
band clears the last value. This does not vote on the biopsy — a rising PSA in a man with a known
diagnosis is the disease behaving as known — it tells the chair how fast the number is moving.
